core_obligations: Reduce to a domain in which the localisation has positive dimension (proof lines 2355-2360).
Choose a nonzero prime not containing the element and a maximal ideal containing it (proof lines 2361-2364).
Use the Zariski pair property to show the two primes differ and that the local ring has dimension greater than one (proof lines 2364-2366).
Apply the infinite spectrum result to conclude that the criterion of the lemma is satisfied (proof lines 2366-2368).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to a domain with positive dimensional localisation (proof lines 2355-2360).
Produce two distinct primes via the Zariski pair property (proof lines 2361-2366).
Infinite spectrum and the Jacobson criterion (proof lines 2366-2368).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that localising a Noetherian Zariski pair at an element of its ideal produces a Jacobson ring. The proof uses the dimension one criterion for Jacobson rings: given a prime of the localisation which is not maximal, the author reduces to the case of a domain in which the localisation has positive dimension, finds a nonzero prime not containing the chosen element, extends it to a maximal ideal, and uses the Zariski pair property to put the element's ideal inside that maximal ideal. The two primes are then distinct and the local ring at the maximal ideal has dimension at least two, so the spectrum of the localisation is infinite by the standard result on opens of spectra of two-dimensional Noetherian local domains, which is exactly what the criterion asks for.
